minutes.headline: Finance Committee skeptical of funding the special ed reserve with free cash before a use policy exists; Collins review scope sent back.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed the draft warrant for the October 22 special town meeting, with the sharpest debate over the special education reserve transfer and the track and field design article. It also discussed a Collins Center scope of work for a budget reconciliation review, which members found too vague, and a DLS educational workshop that would be closed. No formal votes were taken beyond approving minutes and adjourning.

public_comment.topic: Urged transparency on extracurricular and athletics costs, opposed a joint policy letting reserve money flow to the schools without a town meeting vote, proposed fee review, a separate appropriation article, itemized cost schedules, and an invested capital fund.

budget_items.what_was_said: Capital planning season is underway with new submission forms; submissions are due the next day.
A public safety roof project in the FY27 capital plan is out to bid.
figures_as_heard: about a half a million dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: A part-time position would be split between the levy and state aid for libraries, as a possible FY27 omnibus amendment.
Unexpended state aid and other funds could support added town finance capacity; backfilling the reserve was also mentioned.
One FY23 bill from a vendor is expected under the prior-year expenses article.
Out-of-district placements average a high cost and are rising; the reserve would be funded from free cash.
Circuit breaker reimburses only above a multiple of the foundation amount per student, at a share of the cost.
The special ed reserve is capped as a percentage of net school spending.
A member recalled the circuit breaker balance at year end and expected more receipts this year.
The article would move the fee schedule out of the bylaw to the planning board's schedule.
An advisory vote on pursuing demolition; estimated cost is between roughly one and four million.
A member said businesses would pay a large share of stormwater utility revenue versus their share of taxes.
The design and construction administration proposal is for a roughly $2 million project to be funded by borrowing, not free cash or unexpended capital; members doubted the estimate.
The town spends on grass fields annually on maintenance.
A member reported on a net school spending workshop and that Lunenburg spends above the required minimum.

budget_items.topic: Public comment capital and levy proposals
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident listed pending capital needs and proposed a one-time adjustment to fund an invested capital fund.
A resident said athletic fees covered a smaller share of athletics costs and taxpayer share rose.

transfers.description: Proposed transfer of free cash to the special education reserve fund (special town meeting article)
Possible FY27 omnibus budget amendment: part-time teen librarian from levy and state aid, finance office help, backfilling a reserve

decisions.decision: Committee will vote its warrant recommendations at a meeting separate from the public hearing.
Soft deadline of end of month for members to submit questions for the DLS workshop to the town manager.
Feedback to the Collins Center vendor will be held until after the holiday and more member input; the scope will be readdressed at the next meeting.
Planning director will likely not be put on the October 22 agenda; his larger amendments are for May.
Next meeting will mainly be the public hearing on the warrant, and a DLS education session will be scheduled.

what_happened.line: The committee made no recommendation on funding the special education reserve from free cash and set the article for the hearing in two weeks.
Members found the Collins Center scope of work for a budget reconciliation review too vague and held feedback to the vendor until after the holiday.
The committee will vote its warrant recommendations at a meeting separate from the public hearing.
The committee gave no recommendation on the track and field engineering article after a debate over the capital process.
No formal votes were taken beyond approving minutes and adjourning.

why_it_matters: The special education reserve article would be funded from free cash, which the town otherwise uses for other purposes, so residents at the October 22 special town meeting will be asked to vote on it before the committee has taken a position.

The reserve's draw on free cash was discussed without a policy on how the money may be used, and a public commenter objected to any arrangement that lets reserve money reach the schools without a town meeting vote.
